intent: A focused shortcut recorder with engraved keycaps, modifier validation, cancellation and reset, designed for desktop-style app preferences.

layout.direction: A compact shortcut setting with a 26px command icon, 20px label and readable description, followed by a generous dashed recording button containing raised monospaced keycaps. Keep neutral graphite surfaces, 44px targets, a 96px minimum recording target with 16px padding and 12px written feedback beside a separate reset action. Wrap long host key labels and modifier combinations without overflowing the container.
layout.container: Size to the parent with @container. Keep the root width at 100%, capped to the focused component, with 24px desktop and 16px narrow padding.

motion.entrance: Enter the card once with opacity and an 8px rise over 320ms.
motion.interaction: Keep 150ms press feedback on recording and reset controls. No ambient loops.
motion.reduced: Subscribe to live prefers-reduced-motion changes and stop and settle the owned card entrance immediately. Remove press transforms.

responsive.rules: Wrap long copy; stack secondary details inside narrow containers; keep any horizontal scrolling local and keyboard accessible.

accessibility: Use native buttons and form controls with visible 2px focus rings.
Provide labels, meaningful states and polite feedback where actions update content.
Keep IDs instance-scoped with useId; support multiple instances and empty custom data.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion; no automatic action or navigation.

content.defaults: Use the realistic default content from the source; expose content and collection inputs as typed props.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled sequence of KeyboardEvent modifier names followed by the final key. Without onChange, recording and reset are read-only.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial and reset sequence. Local initialization and notifications copy the array.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Synchronous notification containing a separate chord array. The host acknowledges controlled changes, registers shortcuts, resolves collisions and handles unsupported OS combinations.

props.name: theme
props.description: Surface and ink palette; the demo stage follows the chosen theme.

avoid: Remote images, fake network success or hidden external dependencies.
Decorative status badges, gradients as filler, low-contrast text.
Unlabelled controls, hover-only functionality, overflow at 320px.
contract: Preserve ShortcutRecorderProps and the named ShortcutRecorder export. Use defaultValue for local state or value with onChange for controlled acknowledgement. Copy the initial and notification arrays so a callback cannot mutate the stored chord. Controlled values without a writer disable recording and reset.

Record only after deliberate activation of the focused record button. Capture keyboard events on that button rather than globally; typing elsewhere remains unaffected. Ignore composing, Dead, Process and modifier-only key events.

Accept Control, Alt or Meta chords and standalone F1 through F12. Shift alone is not a sufficient modifier. Keep the ordered modifier names Control, Alt, Shift, Meta followed by the final key; uppercase single-character keys. Explain invalid unmodified keys without discarding the current chord or leaving recording mode.

Escape cancels without changing the chord and keeps focus; Tab exits without trapping navigation; blur retires recording. Disabled or read-only changes retire active recording. Reset notifies a copied default sequence and returns focus to the record button.

Keep exact controlled proposals without replacing the host value until it acknowledges. Show recorded/reset feedback only while the actual chord matches that feedback, including after host replacements. Empty sequences have a written not-set label and remain recordable when enabled. Use instance-scoped descriptions and support independent recorders, long labels and separate themes.
onChange is a synchronous chord notification. The host owns global shortcut registration, OS/browser conflicts, validation and persistence. Recording a sequence does not register a shortcut.
